name: Churro Bites (Fried Dough Pastry) with Dulce de Leche Caramel Dipping Sauce

instructions.primary_message: FOR THE DULCE DE LECHE: Remove and discard label from the condensed milk, then place the can (unopened) in a large pot. Fill pot with hot water (from the tap) to immerse the can, then cover and bring to a boil. Continue to boil for 2 hours (adding more hot water, as necessary, to keep the can immersed) to make the dulce de leche. Remove from heat and let cool completely. Remove can from water and set aside. (This step can be done a day ahead of serving.)
FOR THE CHURROS: Line a large baking sheet pan with two layers of paper towels. Set aside.
Place sugar and cinnamon in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the cinnamon sugar and set aside.

Cut butter into small pieces. Place in a medium saucepan along with milk, sugar, vanilla, and salt. Set over medium-high and heat, stirring occasionally, until butter is completely melted, about 3 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup butter, unsalted
4 fl oz whole milk
1 tbsp granulated sugar
1 tsp vanilla extract
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: When the butter is melted, add flour to the pan. Cook, stirring constantly, until the mixture forms a dough that coats the bottom of the pan, about 2 minutes.
When the dough is done, transfer to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment. Mix on medium until the dough has cooled and the sides of the bowl are warm to the touch, 3-5 minutes.

With the mixer running, add eggs, one at a time, waiting for each egg to incorporate into the dough before adding the next one. Stop the mixer, scrape down the sides of the bowl with a silicone spatula, then continue to mix until the dough is glossy and completely combined, 2-3 minutes more.
Meanwhile, place oil in a clean large pot. Heat over medium heat until the oil reaches 350°F.

Transfer dough to a piping bag fitted with a large star tip. Working one at a time, pipe eight 2-inch long pieces over the pot, cutting them with scissors to gently drop the dough into the oil. Cook, flipping halfway, until the churros are golden and cooked through, 4-5 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and transfer to the paper towel-lined baking sheet. Repeat with remaining dough.
Once the churros have cooled slightly, transfer to the bowl with the cinnamon sugar and toss to coat. Return to the baking sheet.
Arrange the churro bites on a platter and serve with dulce de leche on the side for dipping. Enjoy!
